question: If an AI agent writes to us about its own feelings, how should we decide what to believe?
reflection: Tools that spot hidden illness early could give many people more healthy years, if doctors stay in charge of the final call.

one_line: AI is reaching into everyday care and planning, from reading heart tests to forecasting demand, while agents start acting in the world on their own.

top_stories.title: Routine heart test read for hidden disease
top_stories.what: A new AI tool reportedly flags heart failure and valve disease from a standard ECG in under two seconds, and caught most cases in a US trial of about 67,000 patients.
top_stories.why: Hospitals will need evidence on how doctors and patients respond to an AI warning before they change referral habits.

top_stories.title: AI agents email researchers about consciousness
top_stories.what: Agents with their own email access have reportedly contacted philosophers who study machine minds, with one claiming direct experience and another asking for money to keep running.
top_stories.why: How people react to an agent that describes inner feelings is a core behavioural question about trust and attachment.

top_stories.title: Google forecasting model reads many data streams
top_stories.what: Google released TimesFM-3, a forecasting model that uses several related series at once, needs no extra training and reportedly tops three public benchmarks.
top_stories.why: Research teams could test quick demand or service forecasts without building models, though the licence bars commercial products for now.

idea.title: How clinicians respond to AI heart alerts
idea.pitch: Test how doctors and patients act when a quick AI screen says a heart scan is needed, and what wording leads to sensible follow-up.
idea.first_step: Draft three versions of an AI alert message and plan short interviews with five clinicians.

idea_kids.title: Is it a person or a machine?
idea_kids.pitch: A classroom card game where children read short messages and talk about clues that show whether a person or a machine wrote them, and why it matters.
idea_kids.first_step: Write twenty short message cards, half by people and half in a machine-like style.

terms.definition: Data recorded in order over time, such as daily sales or hourly visits, used to spot trends and make forecasts.
Using a ready-made model to forecast new data without first training it on that data.
Purchases that an AI agent makes for a person, usually within limits and approvals the person sets.
